findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: The new cleanup paths unconditionally emit Error-level messages for successful queries and deletes, including the final empty batch. The same issue occurs in count-based cleanup and orphaned-tag cleanup. Consequently, a healthy background job now continually produces error logs and can trigger error-based monitoring alerts; logging every selected ID also makes these messages unnecessarily large. Use debug-level batch diagnostics and reserve error logging for actual failures.

findings.title: Building the SQLite ID list repeatedly copies the entire accumulated string
findings.body: For SQLite batches larger than 999, each iteration formats a new string containing all previously accumulated IDs. This makes statement construction quadratic in the batch size rather than linear. With the 32,767 batch size explicitly supported by the new test, constructing a single delete can allocate gigabytes of temporary strings, adding substantial garbage-collection and CPU overhead to cleanup. Build the list with a strings.Builder or append to a byte buffer instead.
